manualTexts.pg031_n0001: <math><mrow><mpadded lspace="0"><mi>Pi</mi></mpadded><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mtext>Circumference of circular object</mtext><mtext>Diameter of the circular object</mtext></mfrac></mrow></math>
manualTexts.pg031_n0001_easy_read: <math><mrow><mpadded lspace="0"><mi>Pi</mi></mpadded><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mtext>Circumference of a circular object</mtext><mtext>Diameter of the circular object</mtext></mfrac></mrow></math>
manualTexts.pg032_n0033: That is, the circumference of the semi-circle = <math><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>π</mi><mi>d</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></math>.
manualTexts.pg032_n0033_easy_read: That is, the circumference of the semi-circle = <math><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>π</mi><mi>d</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></math>.
manualTexts.pg035_n0005_easy_read: Use <math><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>22</mn><mn>7</mn></mfrac></mrow></math>, unless the question says something else:
manualTexts.pg038_n0017: Thus, area of a circle = <math><mrow><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mn class="tml-sml-pad">2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true" scriptlevel="0"><mfrac><mrow><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>d</mi><mn class="tml-lrg-pad">2</mn></msup></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mstyle></mrow></math>
manualTexts.pg038_n0017_easy_read: So, area of a circle = <math><mrow><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mn class="tml-sml-pad">2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true" scriptlevel="0"><mfrac><mrow><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>d</mi><mn class="tml-lrg-pad">2</mn></msup></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mstyle></mrow></math>
manualTexts.pg038_n0019: Therefore, the area of a circle is given by <math><mstyle displaystyle="true" scriptlevel="0"><mfrac><mrow><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>d</mi><mn class="tml-lrg-pad">2</mn></msup></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mstyle></math> or <math><mrow><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mn class="tml-sml-pad">2</mn></msup></mrow></math> where <math><mi>r</mi></math> is the radius and <math><mi>d</mi></math> is the diameter.
manualTexts.pg038_n0019_easy_read: So, the area of a circle is <math><mstyle displaystyle="true" scriptlevel="0"><mfrac><mrow><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>d</mi><mn class="tml-lrg-pad">2</mn></msup></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mstyle></math> or <math><mrow><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mn class="tml-sml-pad">2</mn></msup></mrow></math>, where <math><mi>r</mi></math> is the radius and <math><mi>d</mi></math> is the diameter.
manualTexts.pg041_n0013: The value of <math><mi>π</mi></math> is 3.141593…, which is approximated to 3.14 to 2 decimal places, and in fraction, <math><mi>π</mi></math> can also be approximated as <math><mfrac><mn>22</mn><mn>7</mn></mfrac></math>.
manualTexts.pg041_n0013_easy_read:
The value of <math><mi>π</mi></math> is 3.141593...
We usually round it to 3.14, to 2 decimal places.
As a fraction, <math><mi>π</mi></math> can also be about <math><mfrac><mn>22</mn><mn>7</mn></mfrac></math>.
manualTexts.pg065_n0015: Fractions with different denominators are fractions whose bottom numbers are different, for example <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math> and <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></math> have different denominators which are 2 and 3.
manualTexts.pg065_n0015_easy_read:
Fractions with different denominators have different bottom numbers.
For example, <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math> and <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></math> have different denominators: 2 and 3.
manualTexts.pg065_n0024: Use colored paper which is in a circular shape like a pizza, cut it into fraction of <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math>, <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></math>, <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math>, <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>6</mn></mfrac></math> and so on.
manualTexts.pg065_n0024_easy_read:
Use coloured paper in a circle shape, like a pizza.
Cut it into these fractions:
- <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math>
- <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></math>
- <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math>
- <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>6</mn></mfrac></math>
- and more
